To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified 7 MC4R variants in obese children and non-obese adult subjects, including 6 missense and 1 silent polymorphisms.
the MC4R missense variants in Polish obese children do not significantly influence obesity risk.
we have found six new MC4R gene missense polymorphisms in Polish obese children (RBMI: 163.6), and that the contribution of these mutations to the pathogenesis and progression of the disease is low.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the first missense mutations in the MC4R coding sequence and the first studies of MC4R gene mutations and polymorphims in Polish obese children.
a new MC4R gene mutation and two new MC4R SNPs in the Polish population.
the first studies of all coding variants of MC4R in obese children and adults from Poland.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MC4R polymorphism is not associated with the RBMI in Polish children and adolescent obese population.
, in the case of the Polish population, the MC4R variants have a minor impact on the pathogenesis of childhood obesity.
the MC4R mutations and polymorphims are of minor importance in the development of obesity in the Polish children and adolescents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MC4R mutations are very rare in Poland and the contribution of MC4R gene to the pathogenesis obesity in Polish children is low.
the MC4R mutations and polymorphs are not the main factors contributing to the pathogenesis and progression of obesity in children and adolescents.
the MC4R mutations in obese children and adults are rare and the protective MC4R mutations are more frequent than those associated with obesity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MC4R variants are not associated with the RBMI in Polish children and adolescent patients with severe obesity.
the MC4R variants are rare and do not contribute significantly to the pathogenesis and clinical features of obesity in the analyzed population.
the MC4R variants are not a major cause of obesity and are not a useful diagnostic or prognostic tool in clinical practice.
